## `64bd7bc767bb` — winner geometry controls count-bar alignment

The exact default remains `alignment_rule=bottom`: independently count colors 1–4 and draw four bottom-aligned bars in output columns 0–3. The nearby `winner_bbox` rule first selects the uniquely most frequent counted color and measures the orientation of that color's input bounding box. A horizontal winner produces top-aligned bars; a vertical winner produces bottom-aligned bars. Thus the renderer consumes an input-derived intermediate rather than a fixed setting-only choice.

The matched-input grammar constructively varies the winning color, both orientations, all four count roles, dense and sparse shapes, ignored colors 5–9, reflections, and sizes through 30×30. Minimum lessons contain both orientations and a lower-count but larger-box decoy. The finite rival audit rejects always-top, color-1 geometry, largest-box geometry, and rank-sorted-count policies. A reusable `audit.py --seeds N --out FILE` command checks matched inputs, setting separation, teaching uniqueness, finite rivals, deterministic support, and stress coverage.

scope: Accepted generator repair; finite reviewer evidence, no new maintainer execution

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The selected chamber rank and cells, plus the local majority color computed inside that selected chamber.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Partition the non-wall cells into chambers, score each chamber by its number of distinct seed colors, and select the unique highest-scoring chamber.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Fill only the blank cells of the selected chamber with that chamber's local majority color, leaving every other chamber unchanged.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The fill region and fill color both come from the selected chamber; using the total-seed winner instead changes the chamber rank, local majority, and final painted cells.
